## Comparability caveat

Alaska Air Group's FY2024 figures are **not** organically comparable to its FY2022/FY2023 figures. Alaska closed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings on September 18, 2024, and consolidated Hawaiian only from that date forward [DOC-2]: "On September 18, 2024, Alaska Air Group completed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings, Inc. ... The results of Hawaiian are included in the consolidated financial statements beginning September 18, 2024. For the period from the acquisition date to December 31, 2024, revenue and net loss from Hawaiian recognized in the Company's consolidated results of operations was $869 million and $113 million, respectively" [DOC-2]. So Alaska's FY2024 revenue includes ~3.5 months of an acquired carrier, while FY2022–FY2023 do not. The other four are clean, like-for-like calendar-year comparisons [DOC-1].

## Growth math

| Airline | FY2022 | FY2023 | FY2024 | FY24 vs FY23 | FY24 vs FY22 (2-yr) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Delta [DOC-1] | $50,582M | $58,048M | $61,643M | **+6.2%** | +21.9% |
| United [DOC-1] | $44,955M | $53,717M | $57,063M | **+6.2%** | **+26.9%** |
| Southwest [DOC-1] | $23,814M | $26,091M | $27,483M | +5.3% | +15.4% |
| American [DOC-1] | $48,971M | $52,788M | $54,211M | +2.7% | +10.7% |
| Alaska (as reported) [DOC-1] | $9,646M | $10,426M | $11,735M | +12.6% (reported) | +21.7% (reported) |
| Alaska (ex-Hawaiian, est.) | $9,646M | $10,426M | ~$10,866M | ~+4.2% | ~+12.6% |

Alaska's adjusted FY2024 figure removes the $869M of Hawaiian revenue recognized post-close [DOC-2] from the $11,735M reported total [DOC-1].

## Interpretation

- **Alaska's headline +12.6% is the largest reported figure, but roughly two-thirds of that increase is inorganic.** Stripping out Hawaiian, Alaska's organic growth (~+4.2%) is the second-weakest of the five, ahead of only American. (Note also that FY2025 will carry a full year of Hawaiian, so Alaska's reported growth will be further inflated by the annualization of the stub period.)
- On a like-for-like basis, **United and Delta are effectively tied on FY2024 year-over-year growth (+6.2% each)**, but United wins on two-year momentum: +26.9% from FY2022 vs. Delta's +21.9% [DOC-1] — United has added revenue faster off its smaller 2022 base in each of the last two years.
- Southwest (+5.3%) is mid-pack; American (+2.7%) is clearly the laggard, with only +10.7% cumulative growth over two years [DOC-1].

**Conclusion:** On a comparable, organic basis, **United Airlines Holdings** showed the strongest revenue growth momentum through FY2024 — matching Delta's FY2024 pace while compounding materially faster over the two-year period. Alaska posted the highest reported growth, but that result is driven by the Hawaiian acquisition and is not comparable to the prior-year base.

ANSWER: United Airlines Holdings — on a comparable organic basis, United had the strongest momentum (+6.2% in FY2024, matching Delta, and +26.9% over FY2022–FY2024, the best two-year growth of the five). Alaska's higher reported +12.6% FY2024 growth is not comparable, as ~$869M of it came from the Hawaiian Holdings acquisition consolidated from September 18, 2024; excluding Hawaiian, Alaska grew only ~4.2%.
